'''Emīlija Gudriniece''' ({{langx|ru|Эмилия Юлиановна Гудриниеце}}; 3 August 1920 – 4 October 2004) was a Soviet and Latvian [[chemist]] who specialized in organic synthesis. She focused on the practical use of substances and synthesized [[Nitrofurazone|furacilin]], for which she won a state prize. She was one of the first to recognize the potential of using vegetable oils as biofuels and initiated the study of rapeseed oil refining in Latvia. She was a prolific publisher, edited the ''Latvian Journal of Chemistry'', and published a Latvian language textbook on organic synthesis methods. She was awarded multiple prizes and recognition for her work.

== Biography ==
Gudriniece was born on 3 August 1920, in the [[Rēzekne district]] of Latvia.<ref name="Latvian Academy of Science">{{cite web|title=Professor Emilija GUDRINIECE|url=http://www.lza.lv/scientists/gudriniece.htm|publisher=Latvian Academy of Science|access-date=29 November 2015|location=Riga, Latvia|date=21 November 2002|archive-date=16 March 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180316083456/http://www.lza.lv/scientists/gudriniece.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref> She grew up in the farming village of Kromoni in the [[Kaunata Parish]] and then went on to graduate from the [[University of Latvia]] in 1948 with a degree in chemical engineering. Gudriniece began her graduate work in 1949,<ref name=bio>{{cite journal|last1=Jure|first1=M.|last2=Strakovs|first2=A.|last3=Avotins|first3=F.|last4=Valters|first4=R.|last5=Kampars |first5=V.|title=In Memoriam: Emilija Gudriniece (August 3, 1920 – October 4, 2004)|journal=Chemistry of Heterocyclic Compounds|date=November 2004|volume=40|issue=11|pages=1513–1515|doi=10.1007/s10593-005-0025-7|s2cid=93641012}}</ref> finishing with her Candidacy Degree in Chemical Science<ref name="LOSI in Russian">{{cite journal|last1=Авотиньш|first1=Ф.|last2=Страков|first2=А.|title=Гудриниеце Эмилия Юлиановна|journal=Химия Гетероциклических Соединений|url=http://hgs.osi.lv/index.php/hgs/article/view/307/261|date=2000|volume=8|issue=398 |pages=1146–1147|access-date=29 November 2015|language=ru}}</ref>{{efn|The Soviet degree, Candidate of Science, was the equivalent of the Western PhD<ref name="Latvian Academy of Science" />}} in 1952. During this same time frame, she won the Latvian Women's Motorcycling Championship twice, both in 1949 and 1953.<ref name=bio /> She was hired as an associate professor that year at the University of Latvia in the Chemistry Faculty, where she remained until 1958. In 1959, she moved to the chemical technology department of the [[Riga Technical University|Riga Polytechnical Institute]] to begin her studies for her [[habilitation]] degree, which was completed from the [[Nesmeyanov Institute of Organoelement Compounds]] of [[Moscow]] in 1960. Following her completion of the advanced degree, Gudriniece was made a professor at the Riga Polytechnic in 1961.<ref name="Latvian Academy of Science" /> She founded the Department of Organic Synthesis and Biotechnology in 1963 at the Polytechnic and headed the department for the next 27 years.<ref name=bio />

Gudriniece's basic research focused on organic synthesis and the practical use of substances for medicines, cosmetics, and industry. She synthesized [[Nitrofurazone|furacilin]] and developed a method of utilizing it for industrial purposes, which earned her the [[Latvian Soviet Socialist Republic]] Prize in 1957.<ref name=bio /> She studied chloromethylated [[nitration]], [[Aromatic sulfonation|sulfonation]],<ref name="Russian bio">{{cite web|title=Гудриниеце Эмилия Юлиановна|url=http://www.biografija.ru/biography/gudriniece-emiliya-julianovna.htm|publisher=Biografija Russia|access-date=29 November 2015|language=ru|date=2006}}</ref> and the reactivity of cyclic 1,3-[[Dicarbonyl|diketones]],<ref name="LOSI in Russian" /> publishing over 600 scientific reports on theoretical and synthetic chemistry of [[Heterocyclic compound|heterocyclic]] and 1,3-dicarbonyl compounds. Her most recent work focused on studies of [[rapeseed]] oil in attempts to develop techniques for the separation of lipids and [[Hydrotreated vegetable oil|refining]] of rapeseed oil as an industry in Latvia.<ref name="Latvian Academy of Science" /> She was one of the first to recognize the application of vegetable oils for [[Biofuel|biofuels]].<ref name=bio /> She also served on the editorial board of the ''Latvian Journal of Chemistry''<ref name="LOSI in Russian" /> and at the time of her death was coauthor of the only textbook in the [[Latvian language]] on organic synthesis methods.<ref name=bio /> Gudriniece received many honors, including the [[Gustavs Vanags]] Prize for Chemistry in 1972,<ref name="Latvian Academy of Science" /> the {{Interlanguage link multi|Vladimir Vasilevich Chelintsev|ru|3=Челинцев, Владимир Васильевич}} Memorial Medal,<ref name=bio /> election as an academician in the [[Latvian Academy of Sciences]] in 1978,<ref name="LOSI in Russian" /> Latvian Emeritus State Scientist in 1996, professor emeritus from the Riga Technical University in 2000, the [[Paul Walden]] Medal in 2000,<ref name="Latvian Academy of Science" /> and the [[Grindeks]] Award for her contributions to education in 2003.<ref name=bio />

Gudriniece died on 4 October 2004, in Riga, Latvia.<ref name="Latvian Academy of Science" />
